chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Fear the bareness (or severing), for it causes men to die.' I said, 'And what is the bareness?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Severing the relationship (of kinship).'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْحَالِقَة: The bareness or severing; a metaphorical term for cutting off kinship ties
key_terms.قَطِيعَةُ الرَّحِم: Severing the relationship of kinship (cutting off family ties)

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'al-haliqah' refer to in Shia hadith and what is its spiritual consequence?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies 'al-haliqah' (the shaver) as a metaphor for severing kinship ties, warning that it causes the premature death of men. This metaphor highlights how the spiritual and physical vitality of individuals is 'shaved away' or diminished by the rupture of familial bonds, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical teachings on maintaining *silat al-rahim*. The warning underscores the severe consequence of this sin, linking social disconnection directly to mortality and loss of life force.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Huzeyfa Bin Mansour who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Fear the bareness, for it causes the men to die’. I said, ‘And what is the bareness?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Severing the relationships’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Be afraid of al -Haliqah; it kills men.’ 1 then asked, ‘What is al-HaliqahV The Imam said, ‘It is failing to maintain good relations with relatives.’”
